subject: Rack seating + IO staging handoff — NorthBay private-cluster preflight
messages:
From: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@northbay.health>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: northbay-devops@northbay.health, alice.tanner@northbay.health
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster preflight — quick questions on node layout and IO staging

Marissa — thanks again for the call this morning. We ran the inventory and have a follow-up set of questions before we lock the landing BOM and sign the reserved capacity addendum. High level: we need a compact 6-rack footprint in a single on-prem room, NVMe-backed local storage for model cache, and an archive tier on our SAN. Specific asks: 

- Can Redwood support split node roles (inference-only nodes + batch/worker nodes) with different PV classes and separate network egress?
- Given the constrained rack count, what guidance do you have for: SSD vs NVMe on inference nodes; ephemeral vs persistent KV cache; and local PV eviction behavior?
- We need to ensure zero-downtime patching for inference pods — what node pool sizing and anti-affinity do you recommend to meet 99.95% availability?

Attached: preliminary BOM and our network sketch. We can share terminal access for a short site readout if helpful. Prefer to get these aligned before Friday so procurement can finalize quotes.

Thanks,
Ben Wallace
Director, Platform Engineering
NorthBay Health
(415) 555-0194

Attachments: NBH-landing-BOM.xlsx (spreadsheet), nbh-network-sketch-v2.pdf (diagram)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@northbay.health>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster preflight — quick questions on node layout and IO staging

Ben — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing our recommendations after a quick ops read:

1) Node roles and PV classes
- Yes — we support distinct node pools: inference (low-latency NVMe), batch (larger CPU/host-local SSD), and control-plane/ops (smaller VMs + NFS/SAN access for artifacts). Use two storage classes: fast-local-nvme (kubernetes local-volume with strict topology) and standard-block-san (CSI to your SAN for archival).
- PV binding mode: for inference caches prefer WaitForFirstConsumer + local persistent volumes provisioned per rack to ensure topology-aware scheduling.

2) NVMe vs SSD and eviction behavior
- Recommendation: inference nodes use NVMe (1–2 TB) for KV cache to hit target p50 token latency. Batch nodes can use enterprise SSDs for cost efficiency.
- Ephemeral cache: safe for transient model warmups; but for fast cold-starts across restarts, use a local PV with replication policy at the application layer (we provide guidance in our runtime docs).
- Eviction policy: reserve 15% headroom on each NVMe node for kube-reserved + eviction thresholds; set kubelet evictionHard for imagefs.available and nodefs.available appropriately and test failure modes during the workshop.

3) High availability and nodepool sizing
- With 6 racks and cost/space constraints, we recommend a 3-failure-domain anti-affinity (spread across 3 rack groups): inference nodepool of 12 nodes (4 per rack-group) with maxUnavailable 1 for rolling updates; batch nodepool of 6 nodes. This sizing gives sustained throughput while allowing one rack maintenance without service disruption (assuming capacity planning for peak QPS).

4) Network and egress
- Separate VLANs for inference traffic (east-west), management/control-plane, and egress; use BGP peering for primary egress plus a secondary egress via fallback region. We can work with your network team to pin IPs and eBGP policies — the attached sketch is helpful.

Next steps: 1) run a 90-minute preflight workshop (we propose Wed 16 Jun 09:00 PT), 2) finalize BOM to reflect NVMe SKUs and 3) capture acceptance test for node eviction and rolling patching.

I copied Jonas (ops) and Irene (delivery) who will own the workshop and acceptance tests. If that time works we will send a calendar invite and a short runbook draft.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: preflight-questions-northbay.md

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: NBH rack constraints & acceptance items

Quick internal notes before the workshop:

- Action: I'll own the eviction/rolling-update acceptance tests. Plan: simulate NVMe saturation and a single rack outage, validate that inference traffic fails over to remaining nodes within target recovery window (we aim for < 30s tail latency increase).
- Action: Irene to draft the runbook for patching with maxUnavailable=1 and signal handlers to drain gracefully. Include drain hooks that pre-warm model cache on target nodes.
- Action: Karthik to confirm CSI plugin compatibility with NBH SAN (they listed Dell PowerStore in BOM). We need driver version and block size guidance.

Risks to call out for the workshop: cross-rack NVMe topology is tricky — local PV WaitForFirstConsumer will pin pods; we should show a demo of our cache-layer replication for fast failover. Also call out the ops requirement for proximity of control-plane to inference VLAN for control-plane health probes.

I'll draft the test matrix and share ahead of Wed.

-Jonas

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@northbay.health>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster preflight — quick questions on node layout and IO staging

Ben/Alice — thanks, we confirmed Wed 16 Jun 09:00 PT for the preflight workshop (calendar invite sent). Agenda attached (short). A few clarifications to help us prepare: 

- Can you confirm whether the SAN will present LUNs to a host cluster or via an existing SAN gateway? That affects our CSI approach and whether we recommend multipath on the worker nodes.
- For operational simplicity, do you prefer a single inference node sku across all racks or a mixed-profile (larger NVMe on 2 racks for hot traffic + smaller NVMe elsewhere)? Mixed profiles add complexity for autoscaling rules.
- Any compliance notes on disk-level encryption (we support KMS/HSM integrations).

We'll bring a short demo of the eviction/restore test and a simple Helm chart that demonstrates WaitForFirstConsumer + PV topology.

Best,
Irene Choi
Delivery Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: preflight-agenda.pdf

From: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@northbay.health>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster preflight — quick questions on node layout and IO staging

All — great, appreciate the fast turnaround and clear plan. Quick answers ahead of Wed: 

- SAN will be presented via gateway; we will email the SAN admin to join the workshop. Expect Dell gateway with multipath.
- We prefer a uniform inference node sku for procurement simplicity (NVMe 2TB per node) — if you can show that meets our latency targets during the workshop that's ideal.
- Disk-level encryption required; we will share KMS contact and policies in the workshop.

See you Wed — Ben

P.S. Alice will push the BOM updates to the shared Drive; Ben W. (cc) will confirm final rack numbering tomorrow.
